jobs.description:

jobs.occupation: Actona - Commercial Excellence Analyst
jobs.description:
Actona Group operates in a dynamic and fast-changing commercial environment, where access to relevant data and the ability to translate it into actionable insights are increasingly important for commercial decision-making. As part of the Pricing & Commercial Excellence team, you will take on a central role in strengthening the commercial organisation through pricing, analytics, performance management and the continued development of commercial tools and processes.

The position combines a strong analytical and hands-on focus with the opportunity to contribute to the broader development of Commercial Excellence across Actona Group.

In this role, you will work at the intersection of data, pricing and commercial decision-making. A key responsibility will be to understand Actona’s pricing model in depth, take ownership of the technical solution behind it and ensure that management decisions related to pricing are effectively implemented. Alongside this, you will identify, collect and analyse relevant commercial data and turn your findings into concrete recommendations and initiatives. You will work with both structured and unstructured data, which calls for an investigative mindset and the ability to find relevant information even when it is not readily available.

At the same time, you will contribute to Actona’s broader Commercial Excellence agenda by developing and evaluating tactical commercial initiatives, supporting performance management and continuously improving the tools and processes that strengthen commercial execution.

Key responsibilities include:

• 
Maintain and further develop Actona’s pricing model and technical pricing solution

• 
Develop analyses, scenarios and decision-support tools to support commercial and pricing decisions

• 
Analyse price and margin development and identify commercial opportunities, risks and areas requiring action

• 
Translate commercial data and insights into concrete initiatives and recommendations

• 
Develop and analyse tactical commercial campaigns and follow up on their commercial impact

• 
Support commercial performance management by identifying opportunities, gaps and areas of underperformance

• 
Prepare clear and decision-oriented material for commercial management and relevant stakeholders

• 
Continuously develop analytical tools, methods and Commercial Excellence processes

• 
Explore how AI and other digital solutions can support commercial analyses, processes and decision-making

• 
Contribute to the implementation of a new CRM system, helping shape commercial processes and strengthen the use of data and insights across the organisation

Success in the role means that you are able to turn complex commercial information into analyses and recommendations that create value for the sales organisation. You drive and coordinate commercial initiatives across the organisation and locations, help sales directors focus and prioritise through relevant analyses, and ensure that pricing decisions are translated accurately and efficiently into the pricing model and commercial execution.

You have experience from areas such as pricing, Commercial Excellence, business analytics, BI, strategy, consulting or finance. You are comfortable working hands-on with data and commercial analysis and, importantly, know how to turn complex information into clear, actionable insights for commercial organisation.

You hold a relevant Master’s degree within engineering, mathematics, economics, business, finance or a similar field. An interest in AI and emerging digital tools is an advantage. You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken, and you communicate insights clearly to different audiences.

They believe in responsibility, collaboration and continuous improvement – and offer a work environment where people are encouraged to challenge, learn, and grow. jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

Fluent English, spoken and written

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant in Learning Design
jobs.description:
The Center for Industrial Software (CIS) at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a Research Assistant position. The position is based at SDU’s campus in Sønderborg and is available from March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is for 12 months.

The position is funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and is part of PREPARE — Pedagogical Alignment for Responsible AI in Software Engineering Education, a joint project between SDU and the IT University of Copenhagen (ITU).

About the position

Generative AI has arrived in our classrooms faster than our pedagogy has adapted to it. Students increasingly delegate the very things we are trying to teach them — verification, trade-off reasoning, judgment, accountability — to tools whose reasoning they cannot inspect. Most institutional responses so far have been restrictions or isolated policies, and neither addresses the underlying problem. This project takes the opposite route: if AI is here to stay in software engineering practice, responsible AI use should be deliberately taught, practiced, and assessed.

This position sits where those ideas become things people can actually use. You will take responsibility for designing and creating content — reusable set of pedagogical modules that instructors can adopt without redesigning a whole course — and for the hands-on work of redesigning selected software engineering courses at SDU. The project’s research produces findings; this role turns them into activities, materials, rubrics, and guidance that survive contact with a real semester. Implementation is iterative rather than one-shot. Modules go into classrooms, evidence comes back through classroom interventions, surveys, artifact analysis, and educator feedback, and the next version is better for it. If you like building educational material and watching it improve under real use — and you would rather serve teaching than only write about it — this is a role with unusually visible results. Responsibility and opportunities

Concretely, you can expect to:

• 
Design and produce reusable pedagogical modules — guided scenarios, reflection and verification activities, assessment tasks, rubrics, and instructor guidance — that courses can adopt on demand.

• 
Redesign selected SE courses at SDU. Work with course responsibles and programme leaders to rework intended learning outcomes, activities, and assessment so that responsible AI use is explicitly taught and examined.

• 
Coordinate classroom deployments across semesters, keeping instructors supported and the logistics from eating the pedagogy.

• 
Gather and act on evidence. Administer surveys, analyze student artifacts (decision notes, verification evidence, reflections), collect structured educator feedback, and feed it into the next iteration.

Excellent written and spoken Danish and English, and the ability to write clearly for two audiences at once: students and the instructors who will use your materials.

Craft in making things others will use. You care whether an activity actually works in week seven of a busy semester, not only whether it reads well in a design document.

A service orientation towards instructors. Course responsibles own their courses and have limited time. We value someone who makes adoption easy and earns agreement through evidence and patience rather than argument.

• 
Organized and self-directed. You will be coordinating deployments across courses at SDU and several semesters, and much of the scheduling discipline will rest with you.

• 
Comfort with iteration. The first version of a module will be wrong in interesting ways. Treating that as information rather than failure is most of the job.

• 
Integrity and care in working with students. You will be collecting data from people who are also being taught and assessed. That asymmetry has to be handled thoughtfully.

The position
The Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), seeks outstanding candidates to fill a number of 3-year assistant professor positions in Quantum Mathematics with emphasis on pure mathematics with relations to quantum theory.
The targeted starting date of the position is 01.08.2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

About the Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM)
Over the past seven years, QM has built a highly international and interdisciplinary research environment spanning a broad spectrum of pure mathematics, mathematical physics and quantum computer science. The Centre has attracted leading international researchers to Odense and developed a unique research environment spanning both fundamental and applied research.

The University of Southern Denmark has recently invested DKK 50 million in the Centre for Quantum Mathematics, on top of its continuous substantial basic funding of the centre, which will enable the Centre to further expand its scientific capacity, attract and retain leading international researchers, increase the acquisition of competitive external research funding and establish strategic collaborations with industry, public authorities and international partners.

As part of this continued development and expansion, QM will move into a new dedicated building from next year. The new building will be located on the SDU campus in Odense and will provide a dedicated research environment for the Centre and its growing international research community.

Research activities and funding
The QM centre is located at the Faculty of Science on the international campus in Odense, Denmark and it is hosting several large European, Danish and American grants including “New Structures in Low-Dimensional Topology” (Simons Collaboration) & “Topological Photonic Quantum Computing and its Applications” (Innovation Fund Denmark) both led by PI and Centre Director Jørgen Ellegaard Andersen; “Mathematics of the open topological string” (VILLUM Investigator) led by Professor Vivek Shende; “The Quantum Geometry of Dynamical Systems” (VILLUM Ascending Investigator) and “The Emergent Geometry of Categories” (DFF Sapere Aude) both led by Associate Professor Fabian Haiden; “New invariants in low-dimensional topology via quantum field theory” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Associate Professor Du Pei, “Global Categorical Symmetries and Phases of Quantum Matter” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Assistant Professor Apoorv Tiwari, “From Pertubative to Non-pertubative Quantum Field Theory by cutting and gluing” (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Assistant Professor Konstantin Wernli and finally “Leveraging Algebraic Geometry for High-Precision Fundamental Physics“ (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Associate Professor Matthias Wilhelm.

A successful candidate will drive internationally competitive research, collaborate with the world community in the field, and attract competitive external research funding. jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Organic and Supramolecular Chemistry: Electrically Controlled Cargo Release in [2]Rotaxanes via Mechanochemical Retro Diels-Alder Reactions at SDU in Odense
jobs.description:
A 3-year (5+3) or 4-year (4+4) PhD position in organic and supramolecular chemistry is available for a highly motivated candidate at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy (FKF) at the University of Southern Denmark. The position is funded by a DFF-Research Project 1 grant from the Independent Research Fund Denmark – Natural Sciences and is available from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
The project focuses on the design and synthesis of electroactive molecular machines capable of converting electrically controlled molecular motion into mechanical force. In particular, the project will investigate whether redox-induced shuttling in mechanically interlocked molecules can be used to trigger the cleavage of covalent bonds and thereby enable controlled cargo release.

Project Background
The aim of this project is to develop electrically responsive molecular machines capable of converting redox-induced molecular motion into covalent cargo release.
Specifically, the project will focus on the design and synthesis of [2]rotaxanes incorporating a redox-active monopyrrolotetrathiafulvalene (MPTTF) unit, a cyclobis(paraquat-p-phenylene) (CBPQT4+) macrocycle, and a furan-based unit linked to a cargo molecule through a Diels–Alder adduct.
Upon electrochemical oxidation of the MPTTF unit, the CBPQT4+ macrocycle is expected to undergo shuttling along the molecular axle. The central hypothesis is that this redox-induced motion can generate sufficient mechanical force to promote a retro-Diels–Alder reaction, resulting in the release of the covalently attached cargo molecule. A key objective is to establish a direct mechanistic relationship between redox-induced macrocycle movement, the generation of mechanical force, and the cleavage of a covalent bond.
The project will involve extensive synthetic organic chemistry, the preparation and characterization of mechanically interlocked molecules, and investigations of their electrochemical and mechanical properties using techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, UV–vis spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry.

By combining synthetic, spectroscopic, and electrochemical studies, the project aims to establish whether electrically driven molecular motion can be harnessed to induce covalent bond cleavage. The results are expected to contribute to the fundamental understanding of force transduction in artificial molecular machines and may provide a foundation for future applications in controlled molecular release.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate holds a Master's degree (5+3 programme) or a Bachelor's degree (4+4 programme) in chemistry or a closely related field, preferably with a strong background in synthetic organic chemistry.

The successful candidate should have:

• 
Extensive practical experience in synthetic organic chemistry.

• 
A strong interest in supramolecular chemistry and molecular machines.

• 
Experience with standard analytical and spectroscopic characterization techniques.

• 
The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment.

• 
Good communication skills and proficiency in written and spoken English.

Previous experience in supramolecular chemistry, mechanically interlocked molecules, or tetrathiafulvalene chemistry would be an advantage but is not a prerequisite.
The successful candidate will also be expected to contribute to the supervision of Bachelor's and Master's students working on research projects within the group.

To learn more about the PhD programme at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, read more here.

jobs.occupation: Tenure-track Assistant and Associate Professorships in Algorithms at SDU Vejle
jobs.description:
We seek candidates to join the Algorithms Section at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science and contribute to the development of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and AI in Vejle.
The starting time is negotiable with a preference for Summer 2027. 

The academic environment
Hired candidates will join the Algorithms Section, which spans SDU’s campuses in Odense and Vejle, and become part of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and AI. Based at the new campus in Vejle, in the heart of Denmark’s Triangle Region and its strong and developing IT ecosystem, the centre offers an inclusive, international and collaborative environment for research and education in Computer Science and AI. It connects research, teaching and innovation through collaboration across research groups and with companies, public organizations and international partners.
The Centre for Computer Science and AI at SDU Vejle connects fundamental computer science with AI, data and advanced digital systems. Its shared focus is how architectures, AI, data and advanced algorithms can transform the specification, design, development, validation, deployment and operation of digital systems. The research environment is also home to SustainAI, an international research group advancing the design, development, evolution, testing and operation of sustainable, high-quality and AI-enabled software systems.
We encourage applications from researchers who can complement or strengthen the Algorithms Section while building links to the centre’s wider scientific environment in areas such as data analytics, data science and machine learning; optimization and computational efficiency; programming languages; software engineering and DevOps; AI-driven development and software evolution; and software architectures, cloud-edge computing, and autonomous and agentic systems.

At SDU Vejle, the department is responsible for international BSc and MSc programmes in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. The programmes provide a strong setting for research-based teaching, supervision, and student collaboration with researchers and external partners.

Research profile
We seek candidates with a strong research record in efficient algorithms, broadly understood as spanning algorithm design, analysis and implementation as well as complexity theory. Relevant areas include, but are not limited to, approximation algorithms, combinatorial optimization, cryptology, data structures, fine-grained complexity, experimental algorithmics, and algorithmic research bridging to machine learning and AI.
Scientific excellence is the primary requirement. We particularly welcome candidates in algorithms engineering, optimization, or computational efficiency, whose work combines strong algorithmic foundations with the design, implementation and rigorous evaluation of algorithms for real-world problems.
Each appointment should help create a clear and distinctive identity for the Vejle environment by building critical mass, adding a missing capability, or creating a strong bridge between research areas. Candidates must strengthen at least one core area and connect meaningfully with other parts of the centre through research, education or external collaboration.

Industrial collaboration
Industrial collaboration is a defining theme of the centre. Successful candidates are expected to demonstrate an interest in engaging with companies and public organizations and the potential to contribute to the digital transformation of industry at local, national and international levels. Relevant activities may include collaborative research, industrial PhDs, student collaborations, and experimentation with industrial data and systems.

Qualifications
Successful candidates for a tenure-track assistant professorship must demonstrate a promising research record within the area of the call and some experience with teaching and supervision at BSc or MSc level. They are expected to contribute to research-based teaching, student projects and thesis supervision, including activities that connect students, researchers and external partners.
The Danish tenure-track system provides a focused pathway toward a permanent academic position. Before the end of the sixth year of employment, and contingent upon a positive academic assessment, the Assistant Professor will transition to a tenured Associate Professor position. Read more about SDU’s tenure-track program here.

The evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential. Emphasis will be placed on the ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. 
As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the tenure evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution. 
The evaluation will also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities. 
Successful candidates for an associate professorship must have an international profile, a distinguished research record within the area of the call, and a proven ability to attract third-party funding. Demonstrated success in building and leading research teams, and a strong record of developing and leading research, innovation or industry-engaged activities, will be an advantage. Extensive teaching and supervision experience across BSc and MSc levels is expected.

Application
In addition to the documentation required under SDU’s appointment procedures, applicants should describe:

• 
Possible existing collaboration with industry or public organizations and plans for developing future external partnerships.

• 
How they would collaborate with existing groups in Vejle, supported by concrete examples of potential research, educational or practical collaboration.

Conditions of employment
Appointment as a Tenure Track Assistant Professor is temporary and for an initial up to 6 years period. 
During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

The Danish tenure track employment
The Danish tenure-track employment is a focused assistant professorship with a guaranteed assessment for a permanent position as an associate professor within the tenure-track assistant professor’s field of study.
The head of department will host annual performance- and development reviews, to ensure the progress of the assistant professor’s development towards meeting the qualifications of an associate professorship. A formal midterm evaluation will be conducted by a committee, consisting of the head of the department and two external researchers with relevant qualifications, with the purpose of ensuring the focus of the assistant professor’s activities, as well as to create the basis for the planning of the remaining period.

To qualify for the position as Tenure Track Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD degree by the employment date.

The transition from assistant professor to associate professor
Within the last year of employment, the tenure-track assistant professor is expected to transition into a position as an associate professor position, based on a positive assessment conducted by a formally approved assessment committee, consisting of a chairman appointed by SDU and minimum one external committee member approved by the dean and the academic council.

Successful applicants to tenure-track assistant professor positions must be scholars with an internationally competitive research profile, whose potential is at the forefront of their discipline. The applicants for tenure-track assistant professorships are assessed based on the criteria of the applicant’s potential to reach an international level of scholarly excellence during the tenure-track period. The candidate will only be promoted to associate professor when the assessment committee confirms that the candidate has scholarly merits at a level of international excellence beyond what can normally be expected for associate professors, with reference to the qualification policy of the research group in which the position is announced.
Indicators of relevant scholarly merits could be documented through scholarly output independent of the PhD supervisor, ground-breaking publications, achievement of excellence grants, and international research network.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellow in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Software
jobs.description:
The position
The Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), seeks outstanding candidates to fill a number of 2-3-year postdotoral positions in quantum algorithms and quantum software.
The targeted starting date of the position is 01.08.2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

About the Centre for Quantum Mathematics (QM)
Over the past seven years, QM has built a highly international and interdisciplinary research environment spanning a broad spectrum of pure mathematics, mathematical physics and quantum computer science. The Centre has attracted leading international researchers to Odense and developed a unique research environment spanning both fundamental and applied research.
The University of Southern Denmark has recently invested DKK 50 million in the Centre for Quantum Mathematics, on top of its continuous substantial basic funding of the centre, which will enable the Centre to further expand its scientific capacity, attract and retain leading international researchers, increase the acquisition of competitive external research funding and establish strategic collaborations with industry, public authorities and international partners.
As part of this continued development and expansion, QM will move into a new dedicated building from next year. The new building will be located on the SDU campus in Odense and will provide a dedicated research environment for the Centre and its growing international research community.

Research activities and funding
The QM centre is located at the Faculty of Science on the international campus in Odense, Denmark and it is hosting several large European, Danish and American grants including “New Structures in Low-Dimensional Topology” (Simons Collaboration) & “Topological Photonic Quantum Computing and its Applications” (Innovation Fund Denmark) both led by PI and Centre Director Jørgen Ellegaard Andersen; “Mathematics of the open topological string” (VILLUM Investigator) led by Professor Vivek Shende; “The Quantum Geometry of Dynamical Systems” (VILLUM Ascending Investigator) and “The Emergent Geometry of Categories” (DFF Sapere Aude) both led by Associate Professor Fabian Haiden; “New invariants in low-dimensional topology via quantum field theory” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Associate Professor Du Pei, “Global Categorical Symmetries and Phases of Quantum Matter” (VILLUM Young Investigator) led by Assistant Professor Apoorv Tiwari, “From Pertubative to Non-pertubative Quantum Field Theory by cutting and gluing” (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Assistant Professor Konstantin Wernli and finally “Leveraging Algebraic Geometry for High-Precision Fundamental Physics“ (DFF Sapere Aude) led by Associate Professor Matthias Wilhelm.

Job description
A successful candidate will help drive internationally competitive research, collaborate with the world community in the field, and contribute to QM’s excellent research environment. The candidates will get the opportunity to shape the development together with the team and implement research project ideas with national and international impact. 
Topics of interest: mathematics, mathematical physics, quantum algorithms, quantum software architecture and quantum computing.

We expect
The candidates must have a PhD degree in pure or applied mathematics, computer science or theoretical physics and a strong research record. 
The candidates must further have an emerging research track in the field. We are seeking highly motivated candidates, who work and communicate well in an international team. The candidates must be able to carry out independent and rigorous work at top international level.
Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Danish is not a prerequisite for application. The hired candidate will be offered Danish courses by the university.

Living and working in Odense
Odense is a fast-growing international community with an open Scandinavian culture, affordable housing and living costs.
